terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: 4 m square commercial patio umbrella on a single centre pole
structureKind: tensioned canvas canopy on radial ribs
motionPotential: none as shipped - the crank and tilt are not modelled
objectClass.notes: The ONE module in the outdoor roof set carried on a SINGLE CENTRE POLE rather than four corner posts, so it tiles differently: placed side by side the canopies meet at their edges and leave the corners open, and the pole lands mid-bay rather than on the grid line. Square rather than octagonal so edges meet cleanly when several are placed together.

reasoning: A canopy surface and a mast; complexity is in the canopy's sag between ribs and the valance rather than in part count.
repetitionDensity 2: eight radial ribs set the sag rhythm, but they are a modulation of one surface rather than separate solids.
actionReadinessNeed 0: the crank and tilt are not modelled, so nothing moves.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Two draw calls of four: the canvas canopy and valance as one double-sided surface, and the mast and base as one merged geometry.

detailInventory.note: Each detail maps to a component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides entry.

details.description: A square hipped canopy, widest at the eave, rising to a small crown at the apex.
The canvas sags between eight radial ribs, so the surface is scalloped rather than a flat pyramid.
A vertical valance skirt hangs from the eave all the way round.
A single vertical tube mast on the canopy axis - the feature that separates this module from the four-post bays.
A round weighted base plate sits flat on the ground and is a trip hazard a player should collide with.
Cream canvas, the brightest surface on the prop, against a duller grey mast and base.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

qualityContract.depthRationale: One mast component plus the canopy as a count-1 repetition system, which is what keeps the canvas on its own material and its own double-sided mesh inside a 2-draw-call build.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Carried on ONE centre pole

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The declared 4 x 4 x 2.8 m governs; the 2.10 m clear height and 2.80 m peak come from the asset notes directly rather than from measuring the plate.
Eight radial ribs, read off the plate's visible seam count on the near faces and assumed 4-fold symmetric.

The canopy is DOUBLE-SIDED rather than a shell with thickness. Canvas has no meaningful thickness at this scale and a player standing under it must see the inside face; building both sides would double the canopy's triangles for nothing.
The crank handle, the tilt joint and the rib hardware are not modelled: they are below the resolvable band at prop distance and the asset declares no moving parts.
The plate's stains and creases are incidental to one worn example rather than properties of the prop, and are not reproduced.
The base is modelled as a plain round weight. The plate shows a cast disc with no visible fixings, and the underside is never visible.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center on the ground at the pole axis, +Y up. The canopy is centred on that axis, so a level builder placing several of these gets the pole mid-bay.

silhouette.description: A square canopy 4 x 4 m at the eave, its corners at y 2.25, rising to a crown at 2.80 with the canvas sagging between eight radial ribs. A valance hangs from the eave down to 2.10, which is the clear height a player walks under. A tube mast r 0.035 runs the full height on the axis, standing on a round weighted base r 0.28 and 0.09 tall.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: The declared 4 x 4 m matches the module grid the rest of the outdoor roof set uses, which divides the kit's 8 m tiles exactly 2 x 2; the asset notes state the 2.8 m peak and the ~2.1 m edge directly, and the eave and valance are placed to land on them.
dominantCurves: the canvas sag between ribs - the only curvature on the prop
negativeSpaces: the whole volume under the canopy, which a player walks through
the open corners left when several are placed side by side

componentTree.name: Tube mast and weighted base
componentTree.topologyRationale: A tube on a cast disc, merged into one geometry because they share a material and neither moves.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 10-segment tube r 0.035 from y 0.09 to the crown at 2.80, standing on a 16-segment disc r 0.28 and 0.09 tall.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The mast passes THROUGH the base disc rather than butting onto its top face, so no two co-facing surfaces are coincident.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry carrying both tones as vertex colours.

localFeatures.description: round base plate on the ground

localFeatures.delivery: double-sided lofted surface, its own mesh

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Vertex colour on one material: pole #99978e, base plate #7b786f.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At base-center on the pole axis. The crank and tilt of a real umbrella are NOT modelled, so one root pivot is the complete mechanism inventory.

collider.notes: Authoring intent only; thaikit derives the shipped compound from the built geometry. The base plate matters here: the asset notes call it a trip hazard a player should collide with.

roughness.notes: Woven canvas: fully matte with no sheen anywhere on the plate. Scalar is the runtime value; textureless.

albedo.samplingNotes: crops/canopy.png measured #dfd8cb at luma 216.8, saturation 0.089 - the brightest surface on the prop and far clear of the harness backdrop's 58, so no lift is needed here. crops/valance.png measured #cdc4b4 at luma 197.0, slightly duller because the valance hangs in the canopy's own shade.

localOverrides.region: the valance skirt below the eave
localOverrides.evidence: Measured 20 luma below the canopy at #cdc4b4. Carried as a vertex colour so the skirt reads as hanging in shade without a second material or any baked shadow in the albedo.

evidence: crops/canopy.png #dfd8cb and crops/valance.png #cdc4b4; the canvas is one tone with a shaded skirt, and the plate's weave is far below the resolvable band on a 4 m canopy at prop distance.
The identity is the SQUARE hipped form, the sag between ribs and the valance - all geometry. The plate's stains and creases are incidental to one worn example rather than to the prop.
Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet; with a texture set the generator would force color to white and roughness to 1 and discard the measured cream.
textureless.note: No textureResolution, referencePbr, textureProjection or surfaceFrequencyBands.

materials.name: Painted tube mast and cast base

roughness.notes: Painted tube, slightly less rough than canvas. Scalar is the runtime value; textureless.

albedo.samplingNotes: crops/pole.png measured #99978e at luma 150.5 and crops/base.png #7b786f at luma 120.0. Both are comfortably clear of the harness backdrop's 58 and neither needs lifting. The material's own colour is WHITE because both tones ride the vertex colour attribute.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/base.png measured #7b786f, luma 120.0 - a cast weight, duller and darker than the painted tube above it.

evidence: crops/pole.png and crops/base.png; two flat tones on parts 70 mm and 560 mm across, with nothing resolvable at prop distance.
Both tones ride vertex colours on one material, so a texture set would buy nothing the attribute does not already carry.
textureless.note: No textureResolution, referencePbr, textureProjection or surfaceFrequencyBands.

repetitionSystems.name: Square canopy and valance

instances.note: One canopy centred on the pole axis.

repetitionSystems.placement: One double-sided canvas surface: 48 perimeter samples lofted from a small crown ring at 2.80 down to the square eave at 2.25, sagging between eight radial ribs, then a valance dropping to 2.10.
repetitionSystems.notes: Count 1 and its own mesh because the canvas is a different material from the mast. Double-sided rather than built with a separate underside: fabric has no thickness, and a player standing under the canopy must see its inside face.

featureReviews.notes: A square 4 x 4 m plan at the eave, not octagonal or round. Built envelope 4.000 x 2.800 x 4.000 m exactly. The square is a requirement rather than a style choice: the asset notes need edges that meet cleanly when several are placed side by side.

One tube mast on the canopy axis and no corner posts, which is what separates this module from the four-post bays in the same set. The pole lands mid-bay, so placed in a row these canopies meet at their edges and leave the corners open.

Valance bottom at 2.10 m and crown at 2.80 m, taken from the asset notes directly rather than measured off the plate. The derived collider confirms it end to end: its canopy slab starts at y 2.09, so a player walks under the rim and stops there.

A round weighted base r 0.28 sits flat on the ground and SURVIVES into the derived compound as its own cylinder part, which is the point - the asset notes call it a trip hazard a player should collide with, and a base that existed only in the render would not deliver that.

The canvas sags between eight radial ribs AND the eave scallops between the rib tips. The scallop was added after the first render: with a straight square eave the shallow canopy read as a flat slab with a skirt round it, which is a fair description of what a 0.55 m rise over a 2 m half-span looks like without it. The rise itself is fixed by the asset notes (2.10 edge, 2.80 peak) and was not changed to flatter the picture.

Valance bottom at 2.10 m and crown at 2.80 m, taken from the asset notes directly rather than measured off the plate. The derived collider confirms it end to end: its canopy slab starts at y 2.09, so a player walks under the rim and stops there.

A round weighted base r 0.28 sits flat on the ground and SURVIVES into the derived compound as its own cylinder part, which is the point - the asset notes call it a trip hazard a player should collide with, and a base that existed only in the render would not deliver that.

The canvas sags between eight radial ribs AND the eave scallops between the rib tips. The scallop was added after the first render: with a straight square eave the shallow canopy read as a flat slab with a skirt round it, which is a fair description of what a 0.55 m rise over a 2 m half-span looks like without it. The rise itself is fixed by the asset notes (2.10 edge, 2.80 peak) and was not changed to flatter the picture.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented.

drawCalls.note: Canopy and valance as ONE double-sided surface, mast and base merged as the second: 2 of 4. The canopy is double-sided rather than built with a separate underside, which halves its triangle count for a fabric that genuinely has no thickness.

materials.note: Canvas and painted metal are different substances with different roughness, so they are two materials. The white pole and the grey base are a COLOUR difference within the metal material and ride vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One canopy surface and one merged mast-and-base geometry.

triangles.note: Measured after the render and recorded here.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: Read off the plate's lit-to-shadow ratio.
Fill ratio taken from the measured lit-face to shadow-face luma ratio.

lightingFromPhoto.source: uniform mid grey studio surround measured off the plate corners
lightingFromPhoto.notes: The seamless backdrop acts as a large source.

lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: A soft ground shadow under the base plate; the canopy's own shade is a property of the geometry and must not be painted into the canvas albedo.
lightingFromPhoto.ambientOcclusion: Contact occlusion in the recesses and under overhangs; lighting, never painted into base colour.
lightingFromPhoto.notes: Exposure and tone mapping intent recorded so a render compares fairly with the plate. No baked lighting or AO enters any albedo.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
